Why now

The road runs one way today

Russians are the largest group of foreign tourists in Türkiye. Turkish tourists in Russia are still rare. That gap is the opportunity.

Russia → Türkiye 6.9 M

Russian tourist arrivals in Türkiye in 2025, the first place among all countries

Source: Interfax, 30.01.2026

Türkiye → Russia 68.7 K

tourist trips to Russia by Turkish citizens in 2025

Source: Interfax, 06.02.2026

To Türkiye
To Russia

About 100 to 1. The Gastronomic Ring builds the road back.

The idea

Tourism exchange must become bilateral

For Russia

What the host country gains

  • Promotion of regions beyond Moscow and St. Petersburg
  • Support for small business: farms, family kitchens, local guides

For Türkiye

What Turkish travellers gain

  • A new destination, close and easy to reach
  • The neighbour’s cuisine, tasted where it was born
Our goal

To strengthen relations between Russia and Türkiye through tourism, culture and gastronomy.

Stronger bilateral ties

Exchange cultural values and build a lasting channel of tourism between the two countries.

New routes

Develop routes across Russian regions that the Turkish audience has not seen yet.

Russia through taste

Show more than beautiful cities: the cuisine, the hospitality and the everyday traditions of Russian, Caucasian and Volga peoples.

Key idea

Cuisine is a universal language. Through food a traveller gets closer to Russia, and Russia gets closer to Türkiye.

Signature routes

Two rings, eight tables

Each ring covers four cities in eight days by comfortable coach, with carefully selected hotels along the way.

Stop 1 · Caspian

Republic of Dagestan

Khinkal, chudu, urbech

Stop 2 · Mountains

Chechen Republic

National dishes and famous Caucasian hospitality

Stop 3 · Black Sea

Gelendzhik

Seafood cuisine and local winemaking

Stop 4 · Resort

Sochi

Black Sea cuisine and a resort finale

Taste glossary

The menu of the journey

Eight dishes guests will meet on the road, and what they actually are.

Khinkal

Republic of Dagestan

Pieces of soft dough boiled in meat broth, served with the meat and a garlic sauce.

Chak-chak

Kazan

Small pieces of fried dough bound together with hot honey. The best-known Tatar sweet.

Chudu

Republic of Dagestan

A thin flat pie filled with meat, cheese or fresh greens.

Echpochmak

Kazan

A triangular Tatar pie with meat, onion and potato baked inside.

Urbech

Republic of Dagestan

A thick paste of ground seeds or nuts, often eaten with honey and butter.

Balesh

Kazan

A large festive pie with meat and rice, served at celebrations.

Kystyby

Ufa

A thin flatbread folded over mashed potato or millet porridge.

Kumys

Ufa

Fermented mare’s milk, a traditional drink of the steppe peoples.

Our story

More than a route

The Gastronomic Ring is a tourism product and a piece of people’s diplomacy at the same time. Every dinner is a small meeting between two countries.

A bridge between cultures

Guests learn the customs behind each dish.

People’s diplomacy

Real contact between families, not only between states.

Growth for regions

Income for small business and local producers.

Long-term friendship

Guests who return, and bring friends with them.

Welcome to the table
